rationale: Re-review reason: depends_on declared (DI-20 -> DI-19); DI-20 text and test unchanged. Upstream context: DI-19 (require an independent verdict, blocking on unreviewed/unfaithful/partial/stale) is what makes the pin meaningful -- a pin that does not track the live test source would let a stale verdict read faithful. Prior verdict recorded no probes; all probes below newly executed one at a time via rdm story mutation-probe. Clauses: (1) a command to record a verdict for a design input -- record_verdict (the logic behind rdm story verdict) writes the file, asserted out.is_file(); argparse dispatch not exercised (repo-wide acceptance convention; CLI smoke-tested elsewhere, untagged); (2) hash-pinned to the CURRENT verifying-test source -- own test: `test_hash = current_hashes(...)` -> `test_hash = ""` KILLED (the freshly written verdict must reconcile FAITHFUL). BUT the own test's tests/ dir is deliberately empty, so the pin never covers any real test source there: `tests_dir = None` in record_verdict SURVIVED and hash_for dropping test sources (`parts = [di_text.strip()]`) SURVIVED against the own test. The clause is genuinely covered by DI-28's tagged test test_verdict_hash_scope_module_default_function_selectable, which calls the same record_verdict over a real tagged test and requires a later test edit to stale it: both mutants KILLED there (recorded below with that test as selector, so replay re-checks the cross-coverage); (3) rejects an undeclared design input -- `if design_input_id not in {...}: return None` -> `if False:` KILLED (record_verdict('DI-404') must return None). All clauses covered (clause 2 via the DI-28 test, stated explicitly). Recommendation: put a tagged test file in the DI-20 fixture so its own test proves the source pin. Hash scope kept as function (legacy verdict had no hash_scope, honored as function-scoped per DI-28).
